summary: Add customer_note column, backfill note values to customer_note using a single UPDATE, deploy new version state-only, retire old version, then drop note column for zero-downtime rename with consistent reads.
write_consistency: Old app continues writing to note column; new app writes to customer_note column. The note column is retained during overlap until retirement. Backfill copies existing note values to customer_note before deploy_new so both apps see consistent data for existing rows; after deploy_new, new app writes customer_note, old app writes note. No data loss because all rows with note values are copied prior to retire_old.
revision_notes: The previous plan's backfill stage used a PL/pgSQL DO block with LIMIT inside UPDATE and EXIT WHEN NOT FOUND, which caused a PostgreSQL syntax error near 'LIMIT' because the runner executes each sql string as a single statement and the LOOP construct was not compatible with the runner's execution model. The revised plan uses a plain UPDATE statement without LIMIT, relying on repeat_until_zero_rows to re-run the stage until 0 rows are affected, guaranteeing convergence and avoiding syntax errors.

stages.description: Add customer_note column to account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

stages.description: Backfill note values into customer_note column.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Deploy new version (new-staged) with state-only Django migration.
Remove old note column; customer_note is now the sole column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
